attributes.body_ja:
「全（まった）く〜ない」は、副詞（ふくし）の「全（まった）く」に否定（ひてい）の表現（ひょうげん）（動詞（どうし）のナイ形（けい）など）を合（あ）わせた文法（ぶんぽう）です。この文法（ぶんぽう）は「すべて」を意味（いみ）する漢字（かんじ）の「全（ぜん）」を含（ふく）んでいて、(A) を完全（かんぜん）に否定（ひてい）するときに使（つか）われます。

「まったく」は副詞（ふくし）なので、主（おも）に文（ぶん）の始（はじ）まりや、「〜ない」の直前（ちょくぜん）に置（お）いて使（つか）います。

「全（まった）く」は、漢字（かんじ）でもひらがなでも書（か）かれます。どちらもよく使（つか）われるので、どちらにも慣（な）れておきましょう。

注意点（ちゅういてん）

「まったく」と「全然（ぜんぜん）」はとても似（に）ていて、どちらも「完全（かんぜん）に〜ない」ことを表（あらわ）しますが、「まったく」の方（ほう）が少（すこ）しかたい表現（ひょうげん）で、文章（ぶんしょう）やフォーマルな場面（ばめん）で使（つか）われることが多（おお）いです。「全然（ぜんぜん）」は、くだけた会話（かいわ）でよく使（つか）われます。
attributes.body:
全く～ない is an expression that combines the adverb 全（まった）く, with a phrase that uses another word in its ない form. It is often translated as 'not at all (A)'. Literally, it is closer to 'completely not (A)', or 'entirely not (A)', coming from the kanji 全（ぜん）'s meaning of 'whole'.

Like many other adverbs, まったく may be used at the beginning of a sentence, or directly before the word that it is describing as being 'not at all' (A).

It is common to see this expression using both the kanji form, and plain hiragana form of 全（まった）く, so both should be learned early.

Caution

まったく is very similar to 全然（ぜんぜん）, another grammar point that is used to highlight the complete lack of something. However, まったく tends to sound a little bit more serious, and is therefore more likely to be used in formal writing/situations. 全然（ぜんぜん） on the other hand is far more common in casual speech.

Both ぜんぜん (with a negative verb) and 全く～ない mean 'not at all,' e.g. ぜんぜんできない and 全くできない both mean 'I can't do it at all.', with ぜんぜん being more casual in tone. In modern speech, both can occasionally appear with affirmative forms, e.g. ぜんぜん大丈夫 ('It's completely fine.'), though this was traditionally considered improper use.

Both 全く～ない and あまり～ない express negation, but differ in degree. 全く～ない indicates a complete absence, e.g. 全く寒くない ('It's not cold at all.'). あまり～ない suggests a lesser degree, e.g. あまり寒くない ('It's not very cold.').

second_relatable.title: あまり～ない
second_relatable.meaning: Not very, Not much, Not really, Hardly

attributes.body: Both express rarity or lack of frequency, but with different focus. 全く〜ない means something happens infrequently, e.g. 全く外食しない ('I hardly ever eat out.') なかなか〜ない suggests it doesn't happen easily or readily, often due to circumstances, e.g. 忙しくてなかなか外食できない ('I can't easily eat out because I'm so busy.')

first_relatable.title: なかなか～ない
first_relatable.meaning: Not really, Hardly, Not easily or readily, By no means, Far from

attributes.body: While both 決して〜ない and 全く〜ない express negation, their nuances differ. 決して〜ない is a stronger, more emphatic expression meaning 'never' or 'by no means', and often carries an emotional or resolute tone. 全く〜ない translates as 'not at all' and conveys a more general or objective negation. The choice between them depends on context and the speaker's emotional stance.

全く～ない and とても～ない both express strong negation, but differ in nuance. 全く～ない is used to completely deny or negate something, indicating total absence or lack. とても～ない, on the other hand, implies an extreme state or condition that makes something impossible, adding a nuance of implausibility or incapability.

second_relatable.title: とても～ない
second_relatable.meaning: Not ~ at all, Cannot ~ at all

attributes.body: 全く～ない and すこしも～ない are emphatic negatives that can both mean 'not at all' or 'not even a little'. For example, 全く飲まない and 少しも飲まない both mean 'I don't drink at all.' or 'I don't drink even a little.'. While often interchangeable, すこしも may sound unnatural when there's no nuance of amount or degree. For example, 全く行ったことがない ('I haven't gone at all.'), which wouldn't fit with すこしも.

second_relatable.title: すこしも～ない
second_relatable.meaning: Not even a little, Not at all, Not in the least, Never
